reader.where: A session, step by step: intro line 160 ("Earlier in this same session the agent built the fix test-first ... and it has been reviewed."), caption line 170 ("the failing run from earlier in the session"), and line 180 ("Notice two things...")
reader.problem: The Scene gets its "before" from the build session's memory, and it implies the review ran in that same session too. The course's advised flow is different: this Lesson's order is review, then the body (line 202, and the right answer at line 446), and Code review says to review from a clean session. A reader who follows that flow asks for the body in the clean review session, which never saw the failing run. The Lesson never says how to get a real before then, so the reader may accept a body with only an "after", which this Lesson calls a claim. The worked example doesn't model the advice next to it.
reader.evidence: Line 160 and line 170 as quoted. Line 202: "Review before the body." content/lessons/10-code-review.md:214: "**Review from a clean session.** ... Review after `/clear` ... or in a new session." content/lessons/10-code-review.md:229: "Run `/mattpocock-skills:code-review` yourself afterwards, from a clean session." pr/SKILL.md:160-164 asks for a before and after: "Show the exact test that now fails and passes". writing-guide.md:114: "Worked examples must model the advice." Line 180 only repeats captions 166 and 176.
reader.fix: Replace line 180 with: "If you reviewed in a clean session first, as [Code review](/learn/code-review) advises, that session never saw the failing run. Ask for the before anyway: the agent can run the new test against `main`'s code, where it still fails." At line 160, change "and it has been reviewed" to "and you've reviewed it". reader.where: Your part, line 199 ("Doubt the comfortable call most."), and the chat Scene caption at line 174 ("You skim the diff yourself")
reader.problem: The Lesson tells the reader to check the agent's door call against the change, and the right answer to scenario-review-effort (line 360) is "a quick skim". reader.fix: End the line 199 bullet with: "Ask the agent to show you the diff (on GitHub, it's the PR's Files changed tab) and check the call against it."

quiz.where: Checkpoints and Final test, all option lists: e.g. line 73 "On the real site too, because...", line 338 "Yes, because only typing `/pr`...", line 384 "...since `/pr` reads that file.", line 434 "...so merging first changed nothing."
quiz.problem: Wording tell across the whole quiz. Every option with a reason clause (because / since / so) is wrong, and none of the 14 right answers has one. A reader who rules out the options that justify themselves gets down to two choices on preview-separate, door-lasting-fix, scenario-need-to-type, scenario-review-effort, scenario-repo-template and spot-merge-then-test without knowing the content. A second, weaker version of the same tell: every option that opens with "Nothing:", "None:" or "Leave it:" is wrong (lines 362, 370, 382, 400, 420, 430).
quiz.evidence: A script over the Lesson's option lines finds the reason words because/since/so in 11 wrong options: lines 73, 77, 211, 338, 340, 358, 372, 384, 388, 434, 436. They appear in 0 of the 14 right options: lines 75, 148, 190, 213, 334, 352, 360, 376, 386, 396, 412, 418, 432, 446. Line 334 uses a semicolon, not one of these words.
quiz.fix: Give three right answers a reason clause. Each one stays shorter than that question's longest option, so the lint still passes. Line 386: "Say in `CLAUDE.md` how they combine, since every session reads it." (66 characters; option b is 73). Line 432: "The merge migrated the real database, so the check came too late." (65; option c is 81). Line 418: "The door is one-way, since texts can't be unsent." (49; option c is 54). Then cut the reason clause from two distractors. Line 77: "Nowhere. Previews are read-only." Line 340: "No. `/implement` already wrote the body when it committed." The existing feedback lines still fit all five options.

quiz.where: How a change ships, line 39 ("gives each preview its own **database branch**, a separate copy of the database"), checked by Checkpoint preview-separate, option d at line 79 ("In production, but only after you squash and merge.")
quiz.problem: The answer depends on a fact the body never states: data added on a preview's database branch never reaches production, even after the merge. The Lesson calls the copy a "branch" and says (line 36) that merging "folds the branch into main". A cold reader can fairly conclude that a database branch gets folded in too, which makes d look right. The fact appears only in d's feedback ("Merging ships the code and its migrations, not the recipes you added while testing"), so the reader learns it from the feedback, not from the Lesson.
quiz.evidence: Lesson line 39 says only that the copy is separate and that "only the merge runs it [the migration] on the real one". Nothing in the body says the copy's data stays behind. The repo backs the missing fact: docs/adr/0002-neon-branch-per-environment.md describes "a throwaway branch per PR preview", chosen to avoid the "risk [of] test data leaking into production".
quiz.fix: In line 39, after "a separate copy of the database.", add: "It's a throwaway copy that's never merged back, so nothing you add while testing a preview reaches the real site." That is +20 words, taking the prose to about 2,900, under the 3,000 lint cap.

quiz.where: Final test scenario-review-effort, option c at line 362 ("None: a two-way door can be merged unread."), and How Matt and others use it, line 229 ("A small two-way door only needs a light review; every one-way door needs a real one.")
quiz.problem: A sharp reader can defend distractor c from the talk the Lesson cites as the source for line 229. Matt's closing rule is that you don't need to review every two-way door, though every one-way door needs review. So "a two-way door can be merged unread" is roughly Matt's own position for some PRs. The Lesson softens that rule to "only needs a light review", and c's feedback then marks Matt's actual rule as wrong. The right answer, b, is still right by the Lesson's own reasoning (the agent is marking its own homework), but c needs to state that error instead of Matt's rule.
quiz.evidence: The English transcript at https://ai.engineer/talks/LlgiOCmFG_w-fixing-pr-bottleneck (read 2026-10-24) has, at the closing rule: "You really don't need to review every single two-way door." That page's own summary says "not every two-way door needs human review". At 18:14 he says of a localized two-way door that he will "sort of review it a little". The Arabic track LlgiOCmFG_w.ar.json at 22:09–22:15 matches. Lesson sources line 460 cites "the closing rule 21:44–22:14".
quiz.fix: Change option c at line 362 to "None: the agent's door call already settles it." (47 characters; the right answer b is 45, option a 58). Keep its feedback: "The call comes from the agent that wrote the code. A quick look is how you catch a 'two-way' that isn't." To keep line 229 true to the source, reword its last sentence to: "When a door is two-way with a local blast radius, he reviews it only a little, and he closed by saying not every two-way door needs a human review, but every one-way door does."

quiz.where: Goals, line 15 ("it's model-invoked, and it writes only the PR body"), against the Final test, lines 330-450
quiz.problem: No Final test question turns on the second half of goal 2: that `/pr` writes only the body and never pushes, opens or updates the PR. Only the Checkpoint body-only tests it, and Checkpoints don't count towards passing. In the Final test it shows up only as a side point. In scenario-need-to-type, a reader who knows `/pr` is model-invoked picks a without needing this fact. In scenario-stale-body, the right answer d ("rewrite the body and update the PR") covers both steps, so a reader who thinks `/pr` updates the PR itself still picks d.
quiz.evidence: In scenario-need-to-type, option c (line 338) is the only option that mentions pushing, and the "No" side settles the question. In scenario-stale-body, none of the distractors (lines 370, 372, 374) depends on what `/pr` leaves to you. The fact is mentioned only in the right answer's feedback at line 377 ("`/pr` won't put it on the PR for you"). The plugin's docs/engineering/pr.md:51-55 back it: "It writes the body and stops" and "It writes the body at one point in time".
quiz.fix: In scenario-stale-body, replace option b (line 372) with "Type `/pr` again: it rewrites the body and puts it on the PR." (61 characters; the right answer d is 52 and option a 59). Its feedback: "It rewrites the body, but `/pr` only writes. Putting the new body on the PR is a step you ask the agent for." The question then checks that `/pr` writes only the body.

quiz.problem: The reader meets "draft PR" here before the Lesson explains it at line 207 ("a draft (marked not ready for review)"). The gloss "waiting for your approval" doesn't match that later definition. Option a's "that body" has nothing to refer to, because the stem never mentions a body.
quiz.evidence: Line 207 defines a draft as "marked not ready for review". The stem at line 183 mentions only typing `/pr` on a reviewed branch.
quiz.fix: Line 186: "A draft PR on GitHub, marked not ready for review." (50 characters; option c is 52). Line 184: "An open PR on GitHub with the new body."

quiz.where: Final test scenario-stale-body, stem at line 369 ("Reviewers asked for big changes...")
quiz.problem: The stem repeats the trigger words of the Your part bullet at line 203 ("Ask for a rewrite after big changes"), and the right answer repeats its action ("rewrite the body"). The question tests whether the reader recalls that sentence, not whether they can apply it to a new case.
